{{Short description|Italian physicist (1940–2017)}}
[[File:AdalbertoGiazotto2016.JPG|thumb|Giazotto in 2016]]

'''Adalberto Giazotto''' (1 February 1940 – 16 November 2017) was an Italian physicist.

Born in Genoa to musicologist [[Remo Giazotto]], Adalberto Giazotto earned his degree in physics from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]]. He helped design the [[Virgo interferometer]], which first detected [[gravitational waves]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bencivelli|first1=Silvia|title=Onde gravitazionali: è morto il padre di Virgo, Adalberto Giazotto|url=http://www.repubblica.it/scienze/2017/11/16/news/giansotto-181265272/|accessdate=20 November 2017|work=Repubblica|date=16 November 2017|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Onde gravitazionali: è morto il padre di Virgo, Adalberto Giazotto|url=http://iltirreno.gelocal.it/pontedera/cronaca/2017/11/16/news/onde-gravitazionali-e-morto-il-fisico-adalberto-giazotto-1.16125979|accessdate=20 November 2017|work=Il Tirreno|date=16 November 2017|language=it}}</ref> He won the [[Tomassoni awards|Caterina Tomassoni e Felice Pietro Chisesi Prize]], a [[Matteucci Medal]], and shared the [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] with [[Barry Barish]] in 2016.
